content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with [product_name] from GNU/Linux machines and cannot print. On my first machine (i386), I am able to open the print dialog, but when I send a print job, I receive this error after a few seconds: 'An unexpected error occurred. Your data may be inconsistent and subsequent errors may occur. java.lang.NullPointerException: null attribute.' On my second machine (amd64), the print dialog does not open at all, showing only 'Service unavailable.' Both systems use Debian and networked printers over ethernet. Is there any advice on how to resolve this?
Is anyone else experiencing this printing problem with [product_name] on GNU/Linux?

Sorry for the late response, but I use Debian Sid and have no issues with printing. You can try removing or renaming the [product_name]-install-dir/jre folder—this forces [product_name] to use the Java runtime environment provided by your Linux installation. This approach allowed me to run [product_name] successfully on my 64-bit Debian Sid system.

Using Linux Mint 11, x86 architecture. The preview function works, but I am unable to print. If I click on 'print,' a message appears: 'No print service found.' CUPS is installed and printing works in other programs. What could be causing this issue?

analysis.insight_summary: Multiple users report problems printing from [product_name] on different GNU/Linux distributions and hardware architectures, facing issues such as failed print dialogs and various error messages. While one person managed to resolve the printing problem by changing the Java runtime environment on Debian Sid, most users consistently experience failures regardless of their settings.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to provide reliable printing features on GNU/Linux systems, similar to other compatible applications, including consistent access to print dialogs and successful printing to networked printers.
